hook: Fail one of *5* quality tests and a drug's licence could stop instantly
hook_b: Fail one of *5* quality tests and a drug's licence could stop instantly
tldr: A proposed amendment to the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, would let regulators, including TGSAFE in Telangana, suspend a drug's manufacturing licence once a State lab declares it Not of Standard Quality.

beats.what: The five tests: sterility, dissolution, assay of active ingredient strength, impurities and related substances.
beats.why: It follows frequent cases of people being exposed to substandard drugs, sometimes with fatal results.
beats.care: Failed batches would be recalled and quarantined, and production halted until fixes are verified.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Today, a failed test usually leads to a show-cause notice and several steps first; officials say this lag leaves bad batches in circulation.

cards.q: Should a drug licence be suspended before the company gets a hearing?

qs: How would a company dispute a lab result under the new rule?
How often do medicines fail State lab tests in Telangana?

facts.t: The change amends the *Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945*.

steps.e: Root cause analysis + CAPA, then verification to resume

viz.verdict: Production stays halted until the regulator verifies fixes.

viz.l: critical tests: sterility, dissolution, assay, impurities, related substances

cover.label: critical quality tests in the draft rule

learn.t: NSQ = Not of Standard Quality, the label a lab gives a drug that fails tests

watch: Whether the Union Health Ministry adds a re-testing or hearing route before notifying the rule.

sources.name: Telangana Today
sources.title: Failed drug quality tests may trigger immediate licence suspension

fact: Medicines failing *5 critical* quality tests may lose their manufacturing licence immediately
twist: Big pharma groups *IPA, FOPE and CIPI* have opposed the move.
